newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks fall sharply in morning trade.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks fall sharply in morning trade.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks fell sharply in Thursday morning trade, pressured by fears of higher interest rates and concerns that measures may be implemented to cool off the hot property market.
The Hang Seng index was down 170.79 points at 13,284.14. Turnover was HK$2.79 billion after the first hour of trade.
"Hong Kong has a few worries today. It is worried about U.S. interest rates and there is also the worry about speculation in properties," Gilbert Chu, head of research at SocGen-Crosby Securities.

The yield on the U.S. long bond continued to climb overnight. The benchmark 30-year Treasury bond fell 20/32 to yield 6.84 percent. However, Chu said he expected interest rates in 1997 to be stable or move a touch higher.
"We believe that the bond yield should stabilise below seven percent," he added.
Property stocks led the market lower on Thursday.
Sun Hung Kai Properties was off HK$1.75 at HK$93.50 and Henderson Land fell HK$1.50 to HK$74.50.

Some analysts said the government could impose measures to curb escalating prices in the property market. Hong Kong Governor Chris Patten said on Wednesday that the government was "keeping the situation under urgent review".

"Clearly if they poke the bubble then the upside blue sky gets removed. Then the extra gain that people have been factoring into shares prices necessarily gets unwound," said Julian Ings Chambers, in institutional sales at BZW Securities.
Shares in the Cheung Kong group fell after some solid gains this week.
Cheung Kong was down HK$0.75 at HK$74.00 and Cheung Kong Infrastructure slipped HK$0.30 to HK$21.45. Hutchison was down HK$1.50 at HK$59.00 and Hongkong Electric shed HK$0.20 to HK$26.95.
In the banking sector, HSBC Holdings fell HK$1.00 to HK$166.50 and Hang Seng Bank was down HK$1.25 at HK$91.00.
January Hang Seng index futures dropped 125 points to 13,265.
